criteria.criterion: docs/user-guide.md states the DC least-privilege expectation (dedicated service account, PAT scoped to only reconciled projects, Browse Projects / Create Issues / Edit Issues / Add Comments / Link Issues, never an admin token), documents allow_insecure as cleartext-only-if-you-must, ca_bundle key for internal-CA certificates, and resolved_statuses for non-conventional workflows

The ADR exists, is Accepted, and records each rejected alternative (fork-per-deployment, hand-rolled stdlib client, generalizing the store vocabulary now, migrating Cloud onto pycontribs) with its reason
ADR 0035 carries a pointer to the amendment, and all THREE stale statements are corrected — at :111 (layout-diagram comment), :204-205 (prose), and :236-237 (Decision item 6)
The ADR records the OSS-comparison finding [rebar:558e-55ce-d9f1-4fa9]: the seam architecture converged with mature Jira integrations, and every gap found was in operational edges
The ADR states the March 2029 DC read-only date and what it implies for future investment in this adapter
docs/user-guide.md documents selecting the DC backend and installing the extra, and the documented commands have been executed against the J5 harness
docs/architecture.md documents the reconciler.backend choice and the jira-datacenter extra (it mentions neither today) — it is a Scope deliverable and was previously uncovered by any AC

The ADR records that ADR 0035's 'the contract suite certifies a backend' claim is CONDITIONAL on the port being complete and typed, citing the measured evidence (6 declared vs TWENTY-ONE called, 12 absent, a live crash while every static signal was green). The figure is 21, not 15.

The ADR describes RemoteRef.instance as INTENDED design with its gap named and ticketed, NOT as an existing mechanism — grep -rn 'RemoteRef(' src/ returns nothing, and the ADR must not contradict that
